title: A LAND YOU DID NOT LABOR FOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The citizens of Jericho fought against you, as did also the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites and Jebusites, but I gave them into your hands. I sent the hornet ahead of you, which drove them out before you — also the two Amorite kings. You did not do it with your own sword and bow. So I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities you did not build; and you live in them and eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.'" — Josh 24:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God brings His account to its climax with words that should have taken Israel's breath away: "You did not do it with your own sword and bow." The land, the cities, the vineyards, the olive groves — all of it was given. They lived in houses they did not build and ate from fields they did not plant. Everything was grace.

This is one of the clearest pictures in the Old Testament of unearned blessing. God deliberately strips away any ground for boasting. Israel could not point to their swords or their labor and say, "We did this." They could only receive what God had given.

Here we must guard our hearts. This is not a promise that faith guarantees us wealth or an easy life. It is a revelation of God's character — He is a generous Giver whose greatest gifts are never earned. The point is not "obey and get houses"; the point is that all we truly have comes as a gift.

This points straight to the gospel. Our salvation is a land we did not toil for, a gift we could never build. It is by grace, through faith, not by works, so that no one can boast (Eph 2:8-9). Everything that matters most, we receive with open hands. Live today as a grateful receiver, not a proud earner, giving thanks for all you did not deserve.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good things in your life have come to you purely as gifts?
2. How does grace guard you against pride and boasting?
3. Are you living as a grateful receiver or a proud earner before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Generous God, everything I have that truly matters is a gift from Your hand. Guard me from boasting, and make me a humble, grateful receiver of Your grace. Amen.
